title: Hybrid probe admission guidelines and metric contracts
content:
Context:

This is a working doc that captures an alternative approach to speculative decoding admission and model onboarding called the 'hybrid probe' pattern. The goal: allow low-latency probe kernels to emit tentative tokens early while limiting exposure to correctness regressions and kernel incompatibilities by gating final commit to a stricter acceptance path.

Why this doc exists:
- Many speculative-decoding notes focus on kernel fallback and KV coherence; teams keep iterating on slightly different admission contracts. We need a single, implementable guidelines doc that is operationally clear for SRE, runtime, and model onboarding.
- Provide concrete telemetry and rollback triggers so product and ML teams can safely onboard newer model variants and faster kernels.

High level concept: hybrid probe admission
- Step 1: Probe emission. Lightweight kernel (fastpath) performs short-lookahead generation for first N probe tokens or until a confidence threshold. Probe writes ephemeral KV entries (tagged as provisional).
- Step 2: Quality/consistency checks. Telemetry compares probe outputs with a gated commit path (or with offline golden prompt set) within a short window.
- Step 3: Commit or rewind. If checks pass, ephemeral KV entries are promoted and subsequent tokens follow committed execution path; otherwise the system rewinds state and falls back to conservative kernel.

Admission Preconditions (must be true before probe starts):
- Model variant has been through unit acceptance smoke tests (see 'smoke checklist' section).
- Target GPU/kernel has a verified fastpath implementation for the model family and sequence range.
- KV cache warmness >=X% (configured per-topology) OR we accept higher rewind cost.
- Request sequence length estimate < configured probe-seq-threshold (default 64 tokens).
- Request is from a tier/route that allows speculative probes (configured via routing policy).

Probe invariants and KV semantics:
- Provisional KV namespace: every probe write is tagged with a monotonic probe id and 'provisional' flag. This prevents accidental promotion of unvalidated state across requests or sessions.
- Promotion is atomic per-request: either the provisional writes are renamed/promoted to the committed namespace OR they are deleted and the session state rewound.
- Eviction policy: provisionals have a short TTL (e.g., 10s) and lower eviction priority than committed entries. SRE must monitor provisional eviction-induced rewinds.

Metric contracts (what we measure and thresholds for acceptance):
- Latency impact:
  - probe-p50 additional (over baseline no-probe) <= 2ms, probe-p95 <= 6ms for single token emission (soft target).
  - commit-path p95 end-to-end latency increase <= 10% under target load.
- Correctness / divergence:
  - token-divergence-rate (fraction of tokens where probe != commit when both run) <= 0.3% on validation set for admission.
  - semantic-drift-score (eval-level metric on representative prompts) delta <= 0.5 points relative to golden baseline.
- Cost/efficiency:
  - rewind-cost (extra GPU-milliseconds per rewind) tracked and averaged; accept if expected rewinds < 0.5% of requests during canary window.
  - kv-provisional-hit-rate (probe benefit metric) >= 12% on high-locality workloads (shows useful prefix savings).
- Stability:
  - error-rate delta (5xxs and kernel-fallbacks) during canary <= baseline + 0.15%.
  - model-acceptance-score: aggregate combining latency, divergence, and stability; threshold must be > 0.8 for green.

Telemetry events (flat, short names — used by console and alerts):
- spec.probe.started (fields: request_id, model, kernel, probe_id, seq_len_est)
- spec.probe.emitted (fields: probe_id, token_index, token_emitted, provisional_kv_size)
- spec.probe.passed_checks (fields: probe_id, compare_hash, divergence_count, semantic_score)
- spec.probe.rejected (fields: probe_id, reason, rewind_cost_ms)
- spec.probe.promoted (fields: probe_id, commit_latency_ms)
- spec.probe.fallback (fields: probe_id, fallback_kernel, err_code)
- spec.kv.promotion (fields: probe_id, promoted_bytes, session_id)
- spec.kv.eviction.provisional (fields: probe_id, reason)

Suggested event schemas are intentionally small to avoid payload bloat; include selective base64 hashes for output comparison rather than full text.

Acceptance testing (pre-canary):
- Offline batch run on canonical prompt set (10k prompts) with probe enabled. Record divergence and semantic metrics.
- Microbench smoke: single GPU isolated run measuring probe-extra-latency across sequence lengths 8/32/64/256.
- KV coherence fuzz: fuzzed concurrent sessions exercising provisional promotion + eviction to ensure atomicity invariants.
- Fault injection: simulated kernel crash during probe commit to ensure rewind path leaves no permanent provisional state.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Lab stage (team only): 0% production traffic, run long-running batch trials for 48–72h.
- Canary A (1% traffic): 24h baseline window, check metric contracts. If any safety threshold exceeds, automatic rollback.
- Canary B (10% traffic): 48–72h, monitor long-tail and cross-tenant effects (cache pressure).
- Ramp (25 -> 50 -> 100%): step increases every 48h with automated gating.

Automated rollback triggers (immediate rollback):
- sustained error-rate delta > 0.5% for 5 minutes
- token-divergence-rate > 1% on live telemetry for 5k sampled tokens
- probe.rewind_rate > 2% for 30 minutes
- unexpected provisional KV eviction causing state loss > 0.1% of sessions
- model-acceptance-score drops below 0.6 for 30 minutes

Manual rollback considerations:
- human-in-the-loop: Product/ML must be paged for quality regressions that are noisy but borderline (0.3% < divergence < 1%).
- blackbox failure: if the fallback kernel also shows regressions, revert to pinned model-version in Dedicated pools.

Operator smoke checklist (short):
- confirm probe.enabled flag is set only for the intended route
- confirm probe TTL and provisional namespace configured per-topology
- ensure telemetry ingestion pipeline for 'spec.*' events is healthy
- confirm canary routing and percent rollouts are configured in smart-routing rules
- pre-seed golden prompt set for on-the-fly comparison

Open implementation notes and risks:
- Rewind cost: large models and long sequences can make rewinds expensive; consider conservative probe token budget for long requests.
- Cross-request leakage: watch for bugs where provisional state is accidentally promoted across session boundaries; unit tests must assert namespace isolation.
- Eviction storms: under memory pressure provisional entries could be mass-evicted; consider pressure-based backoff that disables probes when provisional eviction rate climbs.
- Telemetry sampling: do not sample too aggressively — need representative samples for divergence without overloading storage. Recommend 1% of requests with adaptive bumping during canary.

CLI snippets and debug commands (examples):
- List provisional entries (dev-only): rwin-kvctl --namespace provisional --session ${SID} --list
- Force-promotion (debug): rwin-kvctl --promote --probe ${PROBE_ID}
- Rewind-simulate (local dev): run_spec_probe --model turing-v2 --simulate-rewind --seq 32

Appendix: quick definitions
- probe token: a token generated by a fastpath kernel that is tentative until promotion.
- provisional namespace: ephemeral KV area used for probe writes.
- commit path: the conservative route (slower kernel, strict KV writes) considered authoritative for final outputs.

Next steps (action items):
- [Avery] formalize event schema registry entries with Observability team (due 2024-11-22).
- [Ravi] add unit tests for provisional namespace isolation (PR target 1823).
- [Sofia] run 10k prompt offline acceptance job and upload results to perf board (due 2024-11-30).
- [SRE] create alerting rule for spec.probe.rejected spikes (low priority -> medium).

Unresolved questions:
- Should promotion be per-token or per-request? Current doc assumes per-request promotion for atomicity, but per-token promotion could unlock more incremental benefits at increased complexity.
- When is it acceptable to use probe in long-running chats where sequence length grows unbounded? Proposed mitigation: per-session budget for probes.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive. If you want a lighter-weight approach (e.g., probe-only with statistical acceptance), add a comment but include a fallback operational checklist.
- Please add any historical incidents you remember where provisional state leaked or caused cross-tenant issues; we want to capture real failure modes in the next revision.
